name: Valvular Pulmonary Stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Valvular Pulmonary Stenosis

criteria.description: Peak systolic gradient across the pulmonary valve ≥ 36 mmHg measured by Doppler echocardiography
Thickened and doming pulmonary valve leaflets visualized on echocardiogram
Systolic ejection murmur heard best at the left upper sternal border

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of echocardiographic evidence of pulmonary valve obstruction with peak systolic gradient ≥ 36 mmHg plus valve leaflet abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cardiac catheterization may be used for confirmation in equivocal cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic ejection murmur at left upper sternal border
searchTerms: heart murmur heard at upper left chest
systolic murmur at left upper sternum
ejection murmur at left upper chest
right ventricular heave felt on chest exam
forceful heartbeat on right chest side

occasional.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to right heart strain
searchTerms: liver swelling due to heart pressure
liver enlargement from right heart failure
swelling and fatigue from right heart failure
fainting with exercise and seizure-like jerks
passing out during activity with convulsions

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; BNP may be elevated in right ventricular strain
imaging: Echocardiogram showing thickened pulmonary valve leaflets with doming and increased peak systolic gradient
Chest X-ray showing post-stenotic dilation of pulmonary artery and right ventricular enlargement
Cardiac MRI for detailed right ventricular assessment
genetic: Usually sporadic; may be associated with Noonan syndrome and other genetic syndromes
other: Electrocardiogram showing right ventricular hypertrophy and right axis deviation

distinguishingFeatures: Obstruction located below the pulmonary valve
Different echocardiographic findings with subvalvular membrane or muscular ridge
Valve incompetence causing backward flow rather than obstruction
Diastolic murmur instead of systolic ejection murmur

references: Maron BJ, et al. Valvular Pulmonary Stenosis. Circulation. 2016;133(22):e123-e131.
American Heart Association Guidelines for the Management of Congenital Heart Disease, 2020.
